questions.question: What was the targeted economic growth rate as per the Sixth Five year plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 5.2.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

**Sixth Five-Year Plan:**

__
 
• The Sixth Five-Year Plan marked the beginning of economic liberalization. Price controls were eliminated and ration shops were closed.
 
• This led to an increase in food prices and an increase in the cost of living.
 
• T**he National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development was established for the development of rural areas on 12 July 1982 by recommendation of the Shivaraman Committee.**
 
• **Family planning was also expanded.**
 
• NCR planning board in 1985 and Integrated Development of Small and Medium Towns (IDMST)
 
• The Sixth Five-Year Plan was a great success for the Indian economy. **The target growth rate was 5.2% and the actual growth rate was 5.7%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Five-Year Plan**:

 
 
• The duration of the plan is **1951-56.**
 
• It was based on the **Harrod-Domar model.**
 
• Its main focus was on the agricultural development of the country.
 
• This plan was successful and achieved a growth rate of 3.6%, more than the target growth of 2.1%.
 
 
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan**:
 
 
• The duration of the plan is **1956-61.**
 
• It was based on the P.C. **Mahalanobis Model.**
 
• Its main focus was on the rapid industrialization in the country.
 
• This plan was successful and achieved a growth rate of 4.3% against a target growth of 4.5%.
 
 
 
• **Third Five-Year Plan**:
 
 
• The duration of the plan is **1961-66**
 
• The aim of this plan was to make India a 'self-reliant' and 'self-generating' economy.
 
• The Plan was a failure in reaching the target growth of 5.6% due to the following factors - Chinese aggression (1962), Indo-Pak war (1965), and severe drought 1965-66.
 
• It was a thorough failure as it achieved a **growth rate of 2.8% against a target growth of 5.6% due to unforeseen events that took place during this tenure.**
 
 
 
• **Fourth Five-Year Plan:**
 
 
• The duration of the plan is **1969-74.**
 
• This plan mainly emphasized growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance.
 
• This plan was a failure and achieved a growth rate of **3.3% only against the target of 5.7%.**
 
• The liberation of Bangladesh and Influx of Bangladeshi refugees and the successive failures of the monsoon are the few problems that made this plan a failure.

__
 
• **The minimum age required for an Indian Citizen to become the president of the country is 35 years.**
 
• The president is the head of the Indian state.
 
• The president is the first citizen of India and acts as the symbol of Unity, Integrity, and Solidarity of the Nation.
 
• The election of the president is not done by the people of the Nation but by the members of the Electoral College.
 
• **To be eligible for the election of the president every citizen has to fulfill certain criteria.**

questions.question: Public debt is burdensome if it ___________ future growth in output.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '__**reduced'.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Public debt** refers to the amount of** money owed by the government to its creditors.**
 
• When the government borrows money to finance its spending, it may have to pay interest on the debt, which can become a burden on taxpayers.
 
• However, the impact of public debt on economic growth is not straightforward. If the borrowed funds are invested in productive assets, such as infrastructure or education, they can boost future economic output.
 
• On the other hand, if the debt is used to** finance current consumption or inefficient programs**, it may not generate enough returns to justify the interest payments.
 
• Therefore,** ****public debt can be burdensome if it reduces future growth in output by diverting resources away from productive investments or by creating uncertainty about the government's ability to repay its debt.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **(magnifies) **is not a suitable term to describe the impact of public debt on economic growth. Magnification implies that the debt has an amplifying effect on growth, which may not always be the case.
 
• **(increases)** is a possible answer, but it does not specify whether the increase in public debt has a positive or negative effect on growth. Therefore, it is not a sufficient answer on its own.
 
• **(expands)** is a synonym of increases and suffers from the same limitation as option 3.

questions.question: In which of the following climates you cannot grow a rubber crop?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**polar climate.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rubber crops require a warm and humid climate to grow, which is not possible in polar climates.**
 
• **Polar climates** are characterized by extremely low temperatures and very little** precipitation, making it impossible for rubber crops to survive.**
 
• **Tropical climates, sub-tropical climates, and equatorial climates **are all suitable for rubber crops as they provide the necessary warmth and humidity.
 
• ** Rubber crops **are mainly grown in tropical regions, where countries like Thailand, Indonesia, and Malaysia are major producers.
 
• ** Rubber is a valuable commodity** used in various industries, including automobile, construction, and healthcare.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tropical climate: **This climate is characterized by high temperatures and humidity throughout the year, with rainfall occurring in the form of heavy downpours. Rubber crops thrive in this climate due to the warm and moist conditions.
 
• **Sub-tropical climate: **This climate is similar to a tropical climate but with milder temperatures and less humidity. Rubber crops can still grow in this climate, but the yield may not be as high as in tropical regions.
 
• ** Equatorial climate:** This climate is characterized by high temperatures and humidity, with rainfall occurring throughout the year. Rubber crops can grow well in this climate, and some of the major rubber-producing countries like Ivory Coast and Nigeria are located in equatorial regions.

questions.question: The Resolution of Non-Cooperation movement was confirmed in the annual session of the Indian National Congress at ___________ in December 1920.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. __Nagpur Session__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• C.R. Das moved the main resolution on Non-Cooperation in the annual session of Congress in Nagpur in 1920.
 
• In Nagpur session Congress decided to have the attainment of Swaraj through peaceful and legitimate means, thus committing itself to an extra-constitutional mass struggle.
 
• A program of the surrender of titles, the boycott of schools, courts and councils, the boycott of foreign goods, the promotion maintenance of Hindu-Muslim unity, and strict non-violence was adopted.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi gave up the Kaiser-I-Hind title granted to him by the British government.
 
• A nationwide tour was taken up by Mahatma Gandhi and Ali Brothers of the Khilafat movement, C R Das. Moti Lal Nehru, M.R Jayakar. Saifuddin Kitchlew (Punjab), Vallabhai Patel, C. Rajagopalachari.
 
• T. Prakasam and Asaf Ali left their legal practice and jumped in the full-fledged politics of congress. 
 
• The Non-cooperation movement was the first nationwide mass movement. The year 1921-22 witnessed an unprecedented movement in the nation’s history when there was widespread unrest among students.
 
• A Congress-Khilafat procession took place at Chauri Chaura in the U.P. district of Gorakhpur on February 5, 1922 where 22 police officers were killed by the mob.
 
• Gandhi was profoundly disturbed by the Chauri Chaura incident news.
 
• Gandhi decided to withdraw the movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Madras (now Chennai)** was the venue for the annual session of the Indian National Congress in 1927, where the famous Nehru Report was adopted.
 
• **Bhopal,** the capital city of the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh, has never hosted an annual session of the Indian National Congress.
 
• **Surat** was the venue for the annual session of the Indian National Congress in 1907, which witnessed the famous split in the Congress between the moderates and the extremists.

questions.question: The Sattriya dance, one of the classical dances of India depicts the teachings of which of the following religions?

__
 
• ** Sattriya dance **is one of the eight classical dances of India, which** originated in Assam.**
 
• It was developed in the Vaishnavite monasteries of Assam and is based on the** teachings of Hinduism.**
 
• The dance form was founded by Saint Srimanta Sankardeva, who was a **15th-century Assamese saint, scholar, and social reformer.**
 
• Sattriya dance is usually performed as a part of r**eligious ceremonies and festivals in Assam, **and it typically depicts stories from the Hindu epics and mythology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sikhism:** It is a monotheistic religion founded in the 15th century in Punjab, India, by Guru Nanak. The Sikh culture is known for its music, dance, and martial arts, but Sattriya dance is not a part of it.
 
• **Jainism:** It is an ancient Indian religion that emphasizes non-violence, self-control, and spiritual development. Jainism has its own distinct style of music and dance, but Sattriya dance is not related to it.
 
• **Buddhism:** It is a religion that originated in ancient India and is based on the teachings of Gautama Buddha. Buddhism has its own forms of music and dance, but Sattriya dance is not associated with it.

questions.question: What obstructs the South-West monsoon winds which come from the Arabian Sea while flowing towards the Intertropical Convergence Zone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Western Ghats.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Western Ghats (Sahyadri Hills) obstruct the South-West Monsoon winds coming from the Arabian Sea while they flow towards the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) ✅
 
• **Explanation:**
 
 
• The Southwest Monsoon Arabian Sea branch strikes the Western Ghats almost at right angles.
 
• The high mountain barrier forces the moist winds to rise orographically, causing heavy rainfall on the windward side (Konkan, Karnataka, Kerala).
 
• The leeward side (rain-shadow region), such as interior Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, receives much less rainfall.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Tamil Nadu receives rainfall from Northeast trade winds.

__
 
• From early June to mid-September, between 100- 120 days is the duration of the monsoon. Some places like Tamil Nadu receive a major portion of its rainfall during October and November, but most parts of the country receive rainfall from June to September.
 
• During the winter season, the winds prevailing in the country are the Northeast trade winds.
 
• In major parts of the country, it is a dry season, as the winds blow from land to sea.
 
• When the winds blow from sea to land, it picks up moisture from the sea and brings rainfall to the country.
 
• Due to the geographical location, the east coast receives rainfall as the north east trade winds blow from sea to land in this location. Hence the coast of Tamil Nadu receives winter rainfall.

Monsoon:

 
• Generally, across the world, the monsoons are experienced in the tropical area roughly between 20° N and 20° S.
 
• The climate of India is described as the ‘monsoon’ type. In Asia, this type of climate is found mainly in the south and the southeast.
 
• Out of a total of 4 seasonal divisions of India, monsoon occupies 2 divisions, namely.
 
 
• The southwest monsoon season __- Rainfall received from the southwest monsoons is seasonal in character, and occurs between June and September.
 
• __The retreating monsoon season__ - The months of October and November are known for retreating monsoons.
 
 
 
• Factors Influencing South-West Monsoon Formation
 
 
• The differential heating and cooling of land and water create a low pressure on the landmass of India while the seas around experience comparatively high pressure.
 
• The shift of the position of Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) in summer, over the Ganga plain (this is the equatorial trough normally positioned about 5°N of the equator. It is also known as the monsoon-trough during the monsoon season).

questions.question: Which is the largest Democracy in the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India is the largest democracy in the world which means that India is a democratic country with the largest population in the world.
 
• A democracy refers to a system of government where the citizens exercise power by voting.
 
• The parliamentary system of government is the one in which the executive is responsible to the legislature for its policies and acts.
 
• The Constitution of India provides for a parliamentary form of government, both at the Centre and in the states. *Hence statement A and D are correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• Direct democracy, known as pure democracy, involves citizens directly participating in democratic decision-making.
 
• Direct democracies can function through citizen assemblies, referendums, and initiatives, in which voters vote on issues rather than politicians or parties. India does not follow this.
 
• A recall election (or recall referendum) is a procedure by which voters can remove an elected official from office through a direct vote before their term has ended. There is no mention of recall in constitution of India.

questions.question: The Satavahana kingdom was established about how many years ago?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 2100.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Satavahana kingdom was a dynasty that ruled parts of present-day India from around 230 BCE to 220 CE.**
 
• The kingdom was founded by Simuka, who is believed to have come from a** family of local chieftains in the Deccan region.**
 
• The Satavahanas were known for their patronage of Buddhism and the arts, and their coins featured symbols such as the **chaitya (Buddhist stupa) and the elephant.**
 
• The kingdom's decline was gradual and attributed to factors such as** internal conflicts, invasions by foreign powers, and economic decline.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

Satavahana Dynasty (60 BC-225 AD) -

 
• The Satavahana was an important successor to the Mauryan Dynasty.
 
• Satavahana rule began in the late second century BCE and lasted until the early third century CE.
 
• Although some assign the beginning of their rule to as early as the 3rd century BCE based on the Puranas.
 
• Simuka -
 
 
• Simukha was the founder
 
• Dharanikota near Amravati in Guntur district was the first capital of Simukha.
 
• Simuka was followed by Krishna, under whom the kingdom was extended till Nasik.
 
• ‘Andhras’ mentioned in the Puranas are considered to be identical with the Satavahanas.
 
 
 
• The Satavahanas are also referred to as the Andhras in the Puranas.
 
• According to the Puranas, the Andhras are believed to have ruled for 300 years, which is assigned to the Satavahana Dynasty.
 
• Satavahana Dynasty was an ancient Indian dynasty based in the Deccan
 
 
• Gautamiputra Satakarni -
 
 
• Gautamiputra Satakarni (A.D. 106 – 130) is considered to be the greatest king of the Satavahana Dynasty.
 
• He defeated the Shakas and he claimed that the Kshatriya ruler Nahapana was destroyed by him.

questions.question: Saikhom Mirabai Chanu is an ________

__
 
• Saikhom Mirabai Chanu is an Indian weightlifter.
 
• She has won the World Championships and multiple medals at the Commonwealth Games.
 
• She won India's first medal at the Tokyo Olympics, winning a silver medal in 49kg weightlifting with a total lift of 202 kg.
 
• She belongs to Imphal, Manipur.
 
• She was conferred the Khel Ratna for the year 2018.

• Silver in Tokyo Olympics (49kg)
 
• Bronze in 2020 Tashkent Asian Championships (49 kg)
 
• Gold in 2018 Gold Coast Commonwealth Games (48 kg)
 
• Gold in 2017 Anaheim World Championships (48 kg)
 
• Silver in 2014 Glasgow Commonwealth Games (48 kg)

questions.question: Chemical formula for the marble is _________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __CaCO₃__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__Explanation:__

__
 
• The chemical name of marble is calcium carbonate. 
 
• It has the chemical formula CaCO₃ and is an inorganic chemical compound.

Ca(OH)₂ (aq) + CO₂ (g) → CaCO₃ (s) + H₂O (*l*)

 
• Calcium hydroxide slowly reacts with the carbon dioxide (CO₂) in the air to form a thin layer of calcium carbonate on the walls. 
 
• Calcium carbonate is formed after two to three days of whitewashing and gives a shiny finish to the walls.
 
• Calcium carbonate is a non-toxic, odorless chemical compound that occurs naturally as a white mineral in marbles, limestones, and chalks.
 
• It is one of the most abundant minerals found in the crust of the earth.

Thus, the chemical formula of marble is CaCO3.__

questions.question: ______is the fluid content inside the plasma membrane.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Cytoplasm.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• The cytoplasm is the semi-fluid solution of a cell that is outside the nuclear membrane and inside the cellular membrane.
 
• In eukaryotes (i.e., cells having a nucleus), the cytoplasm contains all of the organelles.
 
• It is mainly composed of water, salts, and proteins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/292e0c96dd6c006ce1f3ef21b86308c7c73a2bc69f508d641b46f352d114f429.png] Important Points__Important cell organelles along with their functions are given below,

 
 

 Organelle
 Main function
 
 

 Cell membrane
 separates the interior of all cells from the outside environment (the extracellular space) which protects the cell from its environment.
 
 

 Cell wall
 The cell wall is a rigid structure composed of cellulose that provides shape to the plant cell, helps keep the organelles inside the cell, and does not let the cell burst from osmotic pressure.
 
 

 Chloroplast (plastid)
 Photosynthesis (traps energy from sunlight)
 
 

 Endoplasmic Reticulum
 Translation and folding of new proteins (rough endoplasmic reticulum), expression of lipids (smooth endoplasmic reticulum)
 
 

 Golgi apparatus
 sorting, packaging, processing, and modification of proteins
 
 

 
 
Mitochondrion

 
 Energy production from the oxidation of glucose substances and the release of adenosine triphosphate(ATP)
 
 

 Nucleus
 Maintains DNA, controls all activities of the cell, RNA transcription
 
 

 Vacuole
 Storage, transportation, help maintain homeostasis
 
 

 Lysosome
 Breakdown of large molecules (e.g., proteins + polysaccharides)

questions.question: _____ intends to provide skill development and placement oriented training across the entire textile value chain, excluding Spinning and Weaving in the organized sector.

options.text: MPLADS (Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Samarth Scheme____.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__ 

__
 
• About Samarth Scheme

 
 
• The Ministry of Textiles is implementing the Samarth-Scheme for Capacity Building in the Textiles Sector.
 
• It is a placement-oriented programme targeting the skill development of 10 lakh youth in the entire value chain of textiles, excluding Spinning & Weaving in the organized Sector.
 
 
 
• Implementing Agencies 
 
 
• Ministry of textiles
 
• Institutions/Organizations of the Ministry of Textiles/State Governments having training infrastructure and placement tie-ups with the textile industry.
 
• Reputed training institutions/ NGOs/ Societies/ Trusts/ Organizations/ Companies /Start-Ups / Entrepreneurs active in the textile sector having placement tie-ups with the textile industry.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• Features of the SAMARTH Scheme

 
 
• Training of Trainers (ToT),
 
• Aadhar Enabled Biometric Attendance System (AEBAS),
 
• CCTV recording of the training programme,
 
• dedicated call centre with a helpline number,
 
• mobile app-based Management,
 
• Information System (MIS) and
 
• on-line monitoring of the training process.
 
 
 
• Objectives
 
 
• To provide demand-driven, placement-oriented National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF) compliant skilling programmes to incentivize and supplement the efforts of the industry in creating jobs in the organized textile and related sectors, covering the entire value chain of textile, excluding Spinning and Weaving.
 
• To promote skilling and skill up-gradation in the traditional sectors of handlooms, handicrafts, sericulture and jute.
 
• To enable the provision of sustainable livelihood either by wage or self-employment to all sections of the society across the country
